```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(mgcv)
library(p8105.datasets)

set.seed(1)
```

```{r}
n_samp = 250

sim_df_const = 
  tibble(
    x = rnorm(n_samp, 1, 1),
    error = rnorm(n_samp, 0, 1),
    y = 2 + 3 * x + error
  )

sim_df_nonconst = sim_df_const |> 
  mutate(
  error = error * .75 * x,
  y = 2 + 3 * x + error
)
```

plot some data

```{r}
sim_df = 
  bind_rows(const = sim_df_const, nonconst = sim_df_nonconst, .id = "data_source") 

sim_df |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = x, y = y)) + 
  geom_point(alpha = .5) +
  stat_smooth(method = "lm") +
  facet_grid(~data_source) 
```

Fit the rergression

```{r}
sim_df_const |> 
  lm(y ~ x, data = _) |> 
  broom::tidy() |> 
  knitr::kable(digits=3)
```

## Draw a bootstrap sample

let's always write a little function

```{r}
draw_boot_sample = function(df) {
  
  sample_frac(df, replace = TRUE)
  
}
```

does this work

```{r}
sim_df_const |> 
  draw_boot_sample() |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = x, y = y)) + 
  geom_point(alpha=.5) + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE)
```

Draw a bunch of samples and analyze

```{r}
#\(i) is fake dataframe to save values and trick map into doing what we want
boot_straps = 
  tibble(
    strap_number = 1:1000
  ) |> 
  mutate(
    strap_sample = map(strap_number, \(i) draw_boot_sample(sim_df_nonconst)), 
    model_fit = map(strap_sample, \(df) lm(y~x, data = df)),
    results = map(model_fit, broom::tidy)
  ) |> 
  select(strap_number, results) |> 
  unnest(results)
```


did this work??

```{r}
boot_straps |> 
  group_by(term) |> 
  summarize(
    mean_est = mean(estimate),
    se_est = sd(estimate)
  )
```

look at results more

```{r}
boot_strap_df = 
  tibble(
    strap_number = 1:1000
  ) |> 
  mutate(
    strap_sample = map(strap_number, \(i) draw_boot_sample(sim_df_nonconst)), 
    model_fit = map(strap_sample, \(df) lm(y~x, data = df)),
    results = map(model_fit, broom::tidy)
  )

boot_strap_df |> 
  select(strap_number, strap_sample) |> 
  unnest(strap_sample) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = x, y = y, group = strap_number)) + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, alpha = .3) + 
  geom_point(data = sim_df_const, aes(group = NULL), alpha = .6)
```


Quick notes

```{r}
boot_straps = 
  sim_df_nonconst |> 
  modelr::bootstrap(n=1000)
```


## Airbnb

This doesnt look good...

```{r}
data("nyc_airbnb")

nyc_airbnb = 
  nyc_airbnb |> 
  mutate(stars = review_scores_location / 2) |> 
  rename(
    borough = neighbourhood_group,
    neighborhood = neighbourhood) |> 
  filter(borough!= "Staten Island") |> 
  drop_na(price, stars) |> 
  select(price, stars, borough, neighborhood, room_type)
```

This doesn't look good

```{r}
nyc_airbnb |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = stars, y = price, color = room_type)) + 
  geom_point()
```


Boot Strap!!

```{r}
airbnb_bootstrap_df = 
  nyc_airbnb |> 
  filter(borough == "Manhattan") |> 
  modelr::bootstrap(n=1000) |> 
  mutate(
    model_fits = map(strap, \(df) lm(price ~ stars + room_type, data = df)),
    results = map(model_fits, broom::tidy)
  )
```

are these coefficients close enough to normal that I can trust default inference? 

```{r}
airbnb_bootstrap_df |> 
  select(results) |> 
  unnest(results) |> 
  filter(term == "stars") |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = estimate)) + 
  geom_density()
```
